groups.title: TypeScript's type system: structural typing and inference
groups.question: An API returns either a list of posts or an error, and a teammate passes an object that was never declared as a Post into a function expecting one, and it compiles. Explain how TypeScript decides what is allowed and how you would model the API result.

followUps.Structural typing: assignability is base: Why does an object that was never declared as a User still pass where a User is expected?
followUps.Discriminated unions and exhaustive type: How does a shared kind field plus a never check make sure you handle every case?

evidence.text: TypeScript checks whether a value has the required properties, not which type name it was declared with.
Any object with at least the right fields and types is accepted.
Object literals written directly get an extra check that rejects unknown properties.

notEnough: Only saying TypeScript is structurally typed.

misconceptions.text: Says an object must be created from a class or declared with the exact type name to be accepted.

evidence.text: Each variant of the union has a common field with a different literal value.
Checking that field narrows the type in each branch, so only that variant's properties are available.
Assigning the value to never in the default branch makes the compiler complain if a new variant is not handled.

notEnough: Only saying it is a union with a type field.

groups.title: Generics, utility types, and async patterns
groups.question: You are writing a helper that reads a field from any entity with an id, and an async function that loads data and catches errors. Explain how you would type both safely.

followUps.Generic functions and the extends constr: What does extends add to a generic function's type parameter?
followUps.Async/await, Promise types, and error ha: Why is a caught error typed as unknown, and what do you do before using it?

evidence.text: A generic lets one function work with many types while keeping the input and output types linked.
extends restricts which types can be passed, for example only types that have an id.
Inside the function you can then safely use the properties the constraint guarantees.

notEnough: Only saying generics make functions reusable.

evidence.text: An async function always returns a Promise of its result type.
A caught error is unknown because anything can be thrown, not only Error objects.
You narrow it, for example with instanceof Error, before reading properties like message.

notEnough: Only saying you wrap it in try and catch.

misconceptions.text: Says a caught value is always an Error object.

groups.title: TypeScript tooling and tsconfig for a T3 project
groups.question: You are setting up a new T3 project and a teammate asks why the build complains about possibly undefined values and why imports look like @/server/db. Explain the key tsconfig choices and how utility types reduce duplication.

followUps.Key tsconfig options: strict, moduleReso: What does strict mode change, and what are path aliases for?
followUps.Utility types: Partial, Omit, Pick, and: How would you create a public user type without the password hash, and an update type with optional fields?

evidence.text: strict turns on checks like strictNullChecks so possibly null or undefined values must be handled.
moduleResolution set to bundler matches how tools like Next.js resolve imports.
Path aliases like @/ replace long relative import paths.
Omit creates a type without chosen fields, such as removing passwordHash.
Partial makes every field optional, which suits update inputs.
Deriving types from one source means changes to the base type flow through automatically.

groups.title: Modern JavaScript patterns used throughout T3
groups.question: A component crashes with 'cannot read property of undefined' while showing a user's avatar, and a new file fails with an import error about require. Explain the modern JavaScript and module features that prevent both.

followUps.ES modules, destructuring, and optional: How does optional chaining stop a crash when a nested field is missing?
followUps.Node.js module system and package.json t: What does setting type to module in package.json change?

evidence.text: Optional chaining returns undefined instead of throwing when a part of the path is null or undefined.
Destructuring pulls the needed fields out of objects and props in one step.
ES modules use import and export with explicit dependencies.

notEnough: Only naming the syntax without explaining what it prevents.

evidence.text: With type module, .js files are treated as ES modules.
That means import and export are used instead of require and module.exports.
Mixing the two systems causes import errors, so the setting must match how files are written.

notEnough: Only saying it enables ES modules.
